text:
devon_support: Customer #C-8742 reporting streaming cut after ~12s idle, then client reconnect gets 403 and we see duplicate billing from retries. They say it started after last week’s Cloudflare Worker roll.
maya_support: Ack — can you drop the minimal repro + logs from the user? any public URL or repro curl?
devon_support: Repro steps from customer:
1) open SSE endpoint for a long-lived chat: `GET /v1/streams/chat?session=...` with `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`
2) leave idle for ~65s
3) client sees silence then reconnect, server logs a 200 then 403 on replay
curl they used:
```
curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/chat?session=abc" 
```
They included this tcpdump snippet (trimmed):
```
12:34:56.789 IP client->edge: GET /v1/streams/chat
12:35:08.123 IP edge->client: chunked 200 OK ... data
12:36:13.456 IP edge->client: <no data> (idle)
12:36:14.001 IP client->edge: FIN (keepalive probe)
12:36:14.010 IP edge->backend: new GET (replay) -> 403
```
maya_support: Interesting — they said ALB in front of our origin and using Cloudflare in front of ALB. ALB idle timeout is 60s by default — could cause half-close.
rory_sre: Can you attach ALB access log lines + Cloudflare Worker trace? the pattern smells like connection reuse + missing auth header on edge replay or a token rotation event.
devon_support: Customer provided ALB log snippet:
```
2026-02-28T12:36:14.010 192.0.2.10:56123 10.0.0.42:443 403 0 0 0 0 123 456 - "GET /v1/streams/chat?session=abc"
```
and Cloudflare worker log shows `fetch(request)` returning 200 first, then on reconnect worker returning 401 because it dropped Authorization on internal retry.
cf_worker_bot: Worker rule: we strip `Authorization` on subrequests when `origin` hostname differs from `x-forwarded-host` unless `preserveHeaders:true`. Pattern seen in 2 recent deploys.
anita_runtime: On our side we also have a short-lived session validation that marks token stale after rotate and returns 403. If Cloudflare strips header on reconnect, origin sees no auth and returns 403 — explains billing duplicates because client retries create new authenticated then unauthenticated attempts.
rory_sre: Two hypotheses:
- H1: ALB half-close after 60s leads client to open a brand new TCP connection to Cloudflare, Worker rewrites headers and drops Authorization => origin returns 403.
- H2: NLB/ALB windowing + Cloudflare TCP coalescing keeps edge alive but our runtime's token cache invalidates on reconnect leading to 403.
maya_support: What concrete repro can we ask customer to run? suggest this minimal curl loop to reproduce locally:
```
# keep a connection open then sleep >60s to trigger idle
TOKEN=<valid_jwt>
curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/chat?session=xyz" &
sleep 70
# open a second connection (simulate reconnect)
curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/chat?session=xyz"
```
maya_support: Also ask them to run `tcpdump -w replay.pcap port 443` during repro and share. rory, I can get their ALB logs.
rory_sre: Meanwhile I'll instrument origin to log `X-Cf-Worker-Auth-Preserved: yes/no` and add a debug header if Authorization present.
anita_runtime: I'll add a temporary metric to count 403 during streaming handoff and a short trace to see whether token cache was checked vs missing header.
devon_support: Customer says they can repro reliably after idle >60s and they confirm Cloudflare Worker was updated around the same time — sounds like a roll introduced header-preserve regression.
maya_support: Mitigation steps we can offer customer:
- Ask them to set client-side shorter keepalive and perform graceful reconnects with `?resume_token=` rather than blind reconnects
- Temporarily set ALB idle timeout >120s (if they control it) OR enable Cloudflare origin keepalive preservation
- Rollback Worker to previous version or set `preserveHeaders:true` on fetch in worker
Provide these in support reply.
rory_sre: Long-term fixes:
- Add a runtime fallback: when Authorization missing on a streaming replay, return 401 with `X-RW-Auth-Missing:1` instead of 403 so clients can differentiate replay vs auth failure
- Instrument end-to-end trace to correlate edge connection ID -> origin request
- Add docs on proxies + idle timeout interplay for SSE endpoints.
cf_worker_bot: Note: Deploy 2026-02-25 changed default fetch behavior; PR #942 toggled header forward. Rolling back or toggling config is fastest.
maya_support: I'll send the mitigation steps + request pcap + ALB logs and mark ticket P2 for now. tagging @rory_sre @anita_runtime for follow-up.
rory_sre: I'll follow up with a tiny origin patch and the extra debug header, will post results here when live.
anita_runtime: ETA for debug patch ~30m, will include a boolean header and metric.
devon_support: Thanks all — will update customer and attach logs when they reply :thumbsup:
